newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkey delays plan for more raw sugar processors.
newsitem.headline: Turkey delays plan for more raw sugar processors.

text.p: Turkey has suspended plans to turn two of its white sugar production plants to raw sugar processing units because of financial difficulties, a senior industry ministry official said.
"We cannot find resources and for this reason the State Planning Organisation (SPO) has not approved the plan," Ersen Yavuz, undersecretary of the industry ministry told Reuters.
"The plan is now under suspension. The conversion of the two plants would cost about $30 million," he said.
State sugar refineries Turkseker, which owns 25 of the 28 plants in Turkey, said last year it would convert its Adapazari and Susurluk plants into raw sugar processors.
Its decision was further supported when it successfully began raws-to-whites production in January, 1996 at its Carsamba refinery on the Black Sea coast with imported raw sugar.
The plant has a daily beet processing capacity of 500 tonnes and aims to export its output.
Yavuz said Turkseker could complete the project in one year if the SPO approved it.
